In fiscal 2019, as a result of lower sales projections in our long range plans for the businesses supporting our Progresso , Food Should Taste
Good , and Mountain High brand intangible assets, we recorded $193 million of impairment charges related to these brand intangible assets (please see Note 6 to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8 of this report for
additional information). 
 In addition, in fiscal 2019, we recorded a $15 million charge related to the impairment of certain manufacturing assets in
our North America Retail and Asia & Latin America segments.

attrs.management_says: Strong free cash flow conversion and disciplined focus on cash (E31, E52).
attrs.numbers_show: CFO was $2,841M → $2,807M (-1.2%, E6, E17, E24) while revenue grew 7.1%. Net income fell 17.8% ($2,131M → $1,753M, E5, E16, E24). The divergence is bridged by non-cash charges: $193M brand impairments (E38), $53M Blue Buffalo inventory purchase accounting (E51), $15M manufacturing impairments (E38), and depreciation ~$620M (E4, E15). CFO resilience matches management's cash-focus narrative.

attrs.management_says: Operations generated $5.6B in cash over the most recent two-year period; we maintained a disciplined focus on cash, resulting in another year of strong free cash flow conversion (E31, E52).
attrs.numbers_show: CFO declined only 1.2% ($2,841.0M → $2,807.0M, E6, E17) despite net income falling 17.8% ($2,131.0M → $1,752.7M, E5, E16). The gap is explained by large non-cash charges (impairments $208M per E38, Blue Buffalo inventory fair-value adjustment $53M per E35, depreciation $620M per E15) and a 34% core working capital reduction (E54) driven by payables extension and lower inventory, which boosts operating cash flow.

attrs.reason: Operating cash flow held nearly flat ($2,841M → $2,807M, E6, E17) while net income fell 18% ($2,131M → $1,753M, E5, E16). The divergence is bridged by disclosed non-cash charges: $193M brand impairments (E38), $53M Blue Buffalo inventory purchase accounting (E51), $15M manufacturing impairments (E38), and ~$620M depreciation (E4, E15), supporting management's cash-focus narrative (E31, E52).

These charges reduce net income but not cash flow, supporting management's cash-focus narrative (E31, E52).
